answers.text: Any digital or computer-assisted post-mortem examination technique

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. This is a common error — 'virtual autopsy' does not encompass all digital techniques.

answers.text: A post-mortem examination conducted exclusively using CT and/or MRI imaging without incision

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Virtopsy (virtual autopsy) specifically refers to the CT/MRI-based non-invasive post-mortem technique developed at the University of Bern. It is not a generic term for any digital autopsy method.

answers.text: A second autopsy conducted when the first is inconclusive

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. A second autopsy on the same body is called an obscure autopsy. Virtopsy refers specifically to imaging-based PM examination.

answers.text: Autopsy conducted remotely by a forensic pathologist via video-link

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Remote video-assisted autopsies are a separate concept; Virtopsy is specifically CT/MRI-based pre-incision imaging.

overallFeedback.feedback: Virtopsy is specifically CT/MRI-based post-mortem imaging, not a generic term for digital autopsies. This distinction is frequently tested.
Correct. Remember: Virtopsy = CT/MRI-based only. Never use it as a generic term for any non-traditional PM examination.
